title: Found in the Archives
notes: Forward with Roosevelt, the blog of the Franklin D. Roosevelt Presidential Library and Museum (NARA), post 'Einstein Letter' on the 2 August 1939 letter.

claim: Albert Einstein signed a letter to President F. D. Roosevelt in August 1939.

evidence.quote:
1939
Einstein signed a letter that informed President F. D. Roosevelt of the possibility of nuclear bombs, warning that the Germans might try to build them.

Because Albert Einstein had a previous personal relationship with the Roosevelts and was internationally well-known for his expertise, a letter informing the President about the dangers of a nuclear chain reaction bomb was drafted for Einstein’s signature.
This August 2, 1939 letter was personally delivered to the President on October 11, 1939

notes: Attribution fact for the direct quotes EIN-F-0082 and EIN-F-0083 (sentences of this letter). IAS says Einstein signed the letter; the FDR Library (NARA) post says it was drafted for Einstein's signature and dates it August 2, 1939. Authorship of the text is shared (LoC EIN-S-0068: drafted by Einstein and Leo Szilard), so captions should say 'signed'.
